classification.difficultyReason: Apply shape descriptions across several displays; the hardest part is interpreting stem-and-leaf row frequencies as a distribution and identifying its tail direction.

content.prompt: Describe the shape of each distribution using the applicable terms: symmetric, positively skewed, negatively skewed or bimodal.

spec.description: Six dot columns with frequencies 3, 10, 5, 3, 2 and 1. A smooth curve peaks above the second column and trails right. The final dot column lies beyond the curve's endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled categorical distribution. Horizontal data values are not supplied. Preserve all 24 dots, the common baseline and the longer right tail; plotting coordinates encode appearance only.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. The classification belongs in the answer.

answer.worked: The peak is toward the left and the longer tail extends toward larger numbers of children, so the distribution is positively skewed.

spec.description: Nine adjoining histogram bars with an overlaid smooth curve. Two approximately equal-height peaks are separated by a trough. Bars are reconstructed without decorative fill.
spec.mathematics: The numerical frequencies and bin boundaries are unspecified. Relative bar heights preserve the source shape. Both bimodality and approximate symmetry are supported.
spec.answerVisibility: Histogram, axes and curve are permanent givens; no classification is printed.

answer.worked: There are two distinct peaks, so the distribution is bimodal. Its overall shape is also approximately balanced about the centre. Either property is valid; both give a fuller description.

spec.description: Horizontal stems with individual leaf digits stacked as graphical data marks above each stem, enclosed by the original rising-and-falling distribution curve. Stem and Leaf labels and the two dividing rules are retained.
spec.mathematics: Stems 0–5 have frequencies 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 5. Bottom-to-top leaves are 0: 8,9; 1: 3,4,6; 2: 2,5,8,8; 3: 4,4,5,7,9; 4: 0,1,1,2,5,6,6,7; 5: 1,1,2,5,9. No key or units are supplied. Curve coordinates are schematic and do not assert an equation.
spec.answerVisibility: All leaf digits and the curve are supplied data. The classification is hidden from the question.

answer.worked: The stem frequencies are $2,3,4,5,8,5$. The peak is toward the higher stems and the longer tail extends toward the lower stems, so the distribution is negatively skewed.
